sections.content:
<tool_call>
<function=python>
<parameter=code>
# Let me try a different approach: move player RIGHT, click 2 green blocks, 
# then try moving UP to see if the player can reach purple blocks

# First move player RIGHT
result = action(['RIGHT', 'RIGHT', 'RIGHT', 'RIGHT', 'RIGHT'])
print(f"Move RIGHT result: gameplay_changed={result.get('gameplay_changed')}")

seg = current_frame.segmentation
nodes = seg['nodes']
player = [n for n in nodes if n['color'] == 'b'][0]
b = player['boundary']
player_r = min(p[0] for p in b)
player_c = min(p[1] for p in b)
print(f"Player at ({player_r},{player_c})")

# Now click 2 green blocks from the right
greens = [n for n in nodes if n['color'] == 'N']
green_positions = []
for n in greens:
    b = n['boundary']
    minr = min(p[0] for p in b)
    minc = min(p[1] for p in b)
    center_r = minr + 2
    center_c = minc + 2
    green_positions.append((center_r, center_c, minc))

green_positions.sort(key=lambda x: -x[2])
print(f"Rightmost greens: {green_positions[:3]}")

# Click 2 rightmost
result = action([{'action': 'MOUSE', 'row': green_positions[0][0], 'col': green_positions[0][1]},
                 {'action': 'MOUSE', 'row': green_positions[1][0], 'col': green_positions[1][1]}])
print(f"Click 2 greens: game_over={result.get('game_over')}, stop={result.get('stop_reason')}")

# Check new state
seg = current_frame.segmentation
nodes = seg['nodes']
player = [n for n in nodes if n['color'] == 'b'][0]
b = player['boundary']
player_r = min(p[0] for p in b)
player_c = min(p[1] for p in b)
print(f"Player now at ({player_r},{player_c})")

# Try moving UP
result = action(['UP'])
print(f"UP result: gameplay_changed={result.get('gameplay_changed')}")

seg = current_frame.segmentation
nodes = seg['nodes']
player = [n for n in nodes if n['color'] == 'b'][0]
b = player['boundary']
player_r = min(p[0] for p in b)
player_c = min(p[1] for p in b)
print(f"Player after UP: ({player_r},{player_c})")
</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>
